segments.flavor: the station signature, landing like a lamp turning
segments.text:
Heart: [gentle] Two hundred miles of dark water, and one lamp turning.
Heart: Lighthouse FM. Stay close to the light, and here is more music.

segments.flavor: the station signature, landing like a lamp turning
segments.text:
Heart: The water is wide tonight and the lamp is patient. This is Lighthouse FM.
Heart: The music is not finished with us yet.

segments.flavor: the station signature, landing like a lamp turning
segments.text:
Heart: Somewhere out past the shipping lanes, someone is still awake.
Emma: So we left the lamp on. Lighthouse FM.
Heart: Music follows, all the way to morning.

segments.flavor: the station signature, landing like a lamp turning
segments.text:
Heart: The tide comes up the stairs and goes quietly back down again.
Heart: We keep the lamp turning. Lighthouse FM, and more music now.

segments.flavor: a slow time check, spoken like a thought, with one image of light or water
segments.text:
Heart: This is the long hour, when the sea forgets which way it was going.
Heart: Nothing here is late anymore. Not you, not the tide. Let the music run.

segments.flavor: a gentle back-announce of the music, like naming a passing ship
segments.text:
Heart: That last piece went by like a ship with its lights held low.
Heart: No name, no flag, only a wake on the water. More of it now.

segments.flavor: a gentle back-announce of the music, like naming a passing ship
segments.text:
Heart: That was a long, slow crossing of a song. One idea, carried the whole way.
Emma: It took its time arriving at the point.
Heart: Everything out here does. The light needs twelve seconds to come back around.
Emma: And here comes the next ship.

segments.flavor: one short reflective thought for night workers, with a soft unexpected smile at the end
segments.text:
Heart: A word for the people awake on purpose tonight. Bakers, nurses, keepers of engines.
Emma: And the ones awake by accident. They also count.
Heart: You are all running the same small errand. Keeping something lit until morning.
Emma: Nicely put. Now play the music, before he writes a poem.

segments.flavor: one short reflective thought for night workers, with a soft unexpected smile at the end
segments.text:
Heart: There is a kind of work that only happens while everyone else is asleep.
Emma: Mine is listening to him find the word for it.
Heart: [chuckle] Loading docks, dialysis wards, two people watching a bridge that never moves.
Emma: All of it invisible again by morning.
Heart: So here is the light, pointed at nobody in particular, and here is the music.

segments.flavor: a slow time check, spoken like a thought, with one image of light or water
segments.text:
Heart: The lamp goes around once every twelve seconds. That is the only clock up here.
Emma: Which makes this a great many seconds after midnight.
Heart: Close enough. The sea has never asked for it more precise than that.
Emma: Nobody has ever missed a wave.
Heart: True. Let the music take the next few turns of the light.

segments.flavor: a slow time check, spoken like a thought, with one image of light or water
segments.text:
Heart: The hour just slid past the place where the names for it stop working.
Emma: It is either very late or slightly early.
Heart: Nicole is on the line, from somewhere the sun has already found.
Nicole: [gentle] It is morning here. The harbour is grey and the gulls are awful.
Heart: So one of us is ahead, and one of us is behind.
Nicole: Same water, though.
Emma: That is the whole show, honestly. Back into the music.

segments.flavor: a gentle back-announce of the music, like naming a passing ship
segments.text:
Heart: We have been running long pieces tonight, one after another, like ships in convoy.
Emma: That last one was the slow one at the back.
Heart: Every convoy has one. Loaded heavy, keeping its own time, arriving when it arrives.
Emma: And nobody signals it to hurry.
Heart: Nobody would dare. The whole point of a convoy is the slowest ship.
Emma: [gentle] Which is a fine thing to be, some nights.
Heart: Here comes the next one, out of the dark.

segments.flavor: a gentle back-announce of the music, like naming a passing ship
segments.text:
Heart: A long stretch of music just went past us, and I did not interrupt once.
Emma: A personal record.
Heart: It came in like a night ferry. Lit windows, nobody on deck, engines very low.
Emma: You could hear where it had been. Salt in the chords.
Heart: Nicole, you get this music out on the far side of the water.
Nicole: We get it later, actually. It arrives about the time our fishing boats leave.
Heart: So it crosses an entire ocean and still gets to work on time.
Nicole: [chuckle] It is more reliable than the ferry.
Emma: Everything is more reliable than the ferry.
Heart: Then we sail on. Here is the next crossing.

segments.flavor: one short reflective thought for night workers, with a soft unexpected smile at the end
segments.text:
Heart: The night shift has its own weather, and it has nothing to do with the sky.
Emma: Hour three is fine. Hour five is a different country with its own laws.
Heart: You never get a visa for hour five. You simply arrive and start apologising.
Emma: To whom?
Heart: The room. The chair. Anyone at all. It is a very polite exhaustion.
Emma: Meanwhile the coffee has quietly given up.
Heart: It did what it could. It is not a miracle, it is a bean.
Emma: A bean with a job, same as the rest of us.
Heart: [gentle] Same as the rest of us.
Emma: Play something kind.
Heart: Something kind, then, all the way to the end of the watch.

segments.flavor: a fake ad for Fathom Wool, a blanket sold by weight
segments.text:
Heart: A word about Fathom Wool, the blanket sold by weight and never by size.
Emma: It is the only blanket with a displacement rating.
Heart: Each one is spun thick enough to hold a person still until morning.
Emma: Fathom Wool cannot be lifted with one arm. Do not attempt stairs while wrapped.
Heart: Fathom Wool. Sink slowly. And now, the music.

segments.flavor: a fake ad for the Low Lamp, a lamp that lights one chair
segments.text:
Heart: The Low Lamp makes one circle of light, roughly the size of a chair.
Emma: Beyond that circle, nothing. The Low Lamp does not believe in the rest of the room.
Heart: Read in it. Sit in it. Let the corners take care of themselves.
Emma: The Low Lamp cannot be aimed, dimmed, or argued with. Bulb sold separately, obviously.
Heart: The Low Lamp. One chair, well lit. Music, out in the dark part.

segments.flavor: a fake ad for Slack Water Tea, a tin with no steeping time
segments.text:
Heart: Slack Water Tea arrives in a plain tin, with no steeping time printed anywhere on the lid.
Heart: Because the answer is always, until you are ready. Slack Water Tea. Steep long, and stay with the music.

segments.flavor: the Ship's Log, one line from a vessel that does not exist
segments.text:
Heart: Time for the Ship's Log. One line, from a vessel that does not exist.
Emma: Tonight's entry.
Heart: Fourth night out. Sea calm. The cook says the bread is winning.
Emma: Winning what?
Heart: The log does not say. The log is not interested in follow-up questions.
Emma: That is the whole entry?
Heart: That is the whole entry. Somewhere a cook is losing to bread.
Emma: [chuckle] Sail on.
Heart: Sail on. Here is the music.

segments.flavor: the forecast for a coast that does not exist
segments.text:
Heart: Now the forecast, for a coast that does not exist.
Emma: My favourite unreliable service.
Heart: Fog on the inner banks until the light comes. Wind light, from nowhere in particular.
Emma: Sea state?
Heart: Long slow swell. Nothing breaking. Nothing that would spill a cup.
Emma: And the outlook?
Heart: Unchanged, for as long as anyone can be bothered to look.
Emma: Perfect. No notes.
Heart: That is the forecast for a coast with no name. Music, over the banks.

segments.flavor: the Word of the Night, an old word from the water
segments.text:
Heart: The word tonight is dogwatch.
Emma: It sounds like a punishment.
Heart: A dogwatch is a short watch, split in two so the crew rotates fairly.
Emma: So nobody always gets the terrible hours.
Heart: Exactly. Someone thought about fairness, at sea, in the dark, and then fixed it.
Emma: With a word. Very sea.
Heart: Dogwatch. Take yours gently. Music, for the rest of the watch.

segments.flavor: one short reflective thought for night workers, with a soft unexpected smile at the end
segments.text:
Heart: To everyone holding a night shift, the dark is not judging your posture.
Heart: It has seen worse. It has seen lighthouse keepers. Back to the music.

segments.flavor: a slow time check, spoken like a thought, with one image of light or water
segments.text:
Heart: Somewhere behind us the hour turned over quietly, the way a page turns in water.
Heart: Nobody signed for it. The lamp went around anyway. Here comes more music.

segments.flavor: a slow time check, spoken like a thought, with one image of light or water
segments.text:
Heart: [gentle] The hour has a number somewhere, but the dark has changed colour twice since.
Emma: It went from ink to something softer.
Heart: That is our clock. Two shades in, one shade left to go.
Emma: Then we are exactly here. Put the music back on.

segments.flavor: a gentle back-announce of the music, like naming a passing ship
segments.text:
Heart: We let that one run long. It seemed rude to interrupt a tide.
Emma: You do not cut in on something that patient.
Heart: Name the next one if you catch it. They go by without introductions.
Emma: Here it comes, low on the water.

segments.flavor: a gentle back-announce of the music, like naming a passing ship
segments.text:
Heart: That one came in slow, low in the water, carrying more than it showed.
Emma: Like a freighter, where you only ever see the top third of it.
Heart: The rest stays under, doing the actual work of the crossing.
Emma: Good crossing. No cargo lost.
Heart: Another is already on the horizon with its lights low. We let it pass through.

segments.flavor: one short reflective thought for night workers, with a soft unexpected smile at the end
segments.text:
Heart: Night work rearranges a person. You start noticing which machines hum in which key.
Emma: The freezer at my old job was in E flat. I am not proud of it.
Heart: You should be. Somebody has to keep the inventory of small sounds.
Emma: [chuckle] It is a short list, and I am the only one on it.
Heart: Then the job is yours. Music, while the freezer holds its note.

segments.flavor: one short reflective thought for night workers, with a soft unexpected smile at the end
segments.text:
Heart: Somebody is awake right now because a machine needs a person nearby.
Emma: Not doing anything. Simply being nearby.
Heart: That is real work. The machine runs better when it is not alone.
Emma: [chuckle] I have the same arrangement with my houseplants.
Heart: Then you understand the job. It is mostly company, and a little vigilance.
Emma: And a thermos. The thermos is doing half of it.
Heart: More than half. We will keep the same kind of company with this.

segments.flavor: a slow time check, spoken like a thought, with one image of light or water
segments.text:
Heart: There is a moment in the night when the building stops settling and simply sits.
Emma: The pipes go quiet. Even the fridge takes a break.
Heart: We are in it now. The whole place is holding one long low note.
Emma: Do not name the hour out loud. You will scare it off.
Heart: [whisper] I will not. I will say only that the lamp is still turning.
Emma: Careful. That was almost a number.
Heart: Nearly. Music now, before I start doing arithmetic at the water.

segments.flavor: a slow time check, spoken like a thought, with one image of light or water
segments.text:
Heart: I stopped keeping the hour a while ago, and nothing came looking for me.
Emma: That is either freedom or negligence.
Heart: Up here they are the same job.
Emma: The kettle still marks the quarters, though.
Heart: The kettle is the most accurate instrument in this building.
Emma: It has never once been wrong. Loud, opinionated, never wrong.
Heart: It has boiled four times since the last time I looked out the window.
Emma: So. Four kettles past the dark.
Heart: [gentle] Four kettles past the dark. I like that better than a number.
Emma: It will never catch on.
Heart: Nothing good does, quickly. More music now, four kettles in.

segments.flavor: a gentle back-announce of the music, like naming a passing ship
segments.text:
Heart: Three pieces went by while we said nothing at all.
Emma: I counted. It was four.
Heart: Four, then. A small fleet, all heading the same direction.
Emma: One of them had a cello in it. Low, like an engine room.
Heart: That was the one that changed the temperature of this room.
Emma: It did. I put a blanket on halfway through and I am not sorry.
Heart: Nobody is asking you to be sorry. That is what the music was for.
Emma: [gentle] Warmth, with strings attached.
Heart: [chuckle] There it is. The one joke, right on time.
Emma: One a night. That is the agreement.
Heart: And it was a good one. Here comes the rest of the fleet.

segments.flavor: a fake ad for the Hourless Clock, a clock face with no numbers
segments.text:
Heart: The Hourless Clock has a face, two hands, and no numbers anywhere on it.
Emma: It tells you that time is passing and declines to say how much.
Heart: Hang it where a clock would go. Notice how little you actually needed.
Emma: The Hourless Clock is not accepted as evidence by any employer.
Heart: [gentle] The Hourless Clock. It has all night, and so does this music.

segments.flavor: a fake ad for Harbor Socks, wool knitted for standing still
segments.text:
Heart: [gentle] Harbor Socks are knitted for people who stand still, which is far harder on the feet than walking.
Heart: Thick, grey, and honest. Sold two pairs to a box, with no returns once worn. Music now.

segments.flavor: a fake ad for Deep Water Blue, a ceiling paint in one shade
segments.text:
Heart: Deep Water Blue is a ceiling paint, and it comes in exactly one shade.
Emma: The colour of the sea at the depth where the light gives up.
Heart: Nicole painted hers with it. Nicole, an honest word.
Nicole: I have not seen my ceiling since. I do not miss it at all.
Heart: Any regrets?
Nicole: One. I did the hallway too. Now the hallway is a harbour.
Emma: One coat covers. Two is a commitment. Three and we cannot help you.
Heart: Deep Water Blue. Look up, and go under. Music, all the way down.

segments.flavor: a fake ad for Ballast, a weighted pillow of river stones
segments.text:
Heart: Ballast is a pillow filled with small smooth stones from a river nobody named.
Emma: It weighs what a cat weighs, and it does not move in the night.
Heart: You put it on your chest, and something in you decides the boat is steady.
Emma: Ballast is not a medical device. Do not place Ballast on a cat.
Heart: [gentle] Ballast. Heavy, in the good way. Let the music carry on.

segments.flavor: a fake ad for the Watch Chair, built for sitting up at night
segments.text:
Heart: The Watch Chair was built for sitting up, not for falling asleep in.
Emma: A subtle difference your spine understands immediately.
Heart: The back is straight. The arms are wide enough for a cup and a book.
Emma: And there is a small shelf for the thing you keep checking.
Heart: One chair, one lamp, one long night. It has done this before.
Emma: The Watch Chair is assembled with a tool that is not included. Good luck.
Heart: The Watch Chair. Sit up, stay warm, and let this next piece play.

segments.flavor: the Lost and Found, things the water gave back
segments.text:
Heart: The Lost and Found. Things the water gave back this week.
Emma: One glove. Left hand. It is always the left hand.
Heart: One bottle, sealed, with sand inside and nothing written at all.
Emma: A message with the message removed. Very modern.
Heart: One wooden spoon, worn thin on one side. Somebody stirred with that for years.
Emma: And one shoe, which we are not going to describe further.
Heart: The sea keeps what it likes and returns the rest. Claims at the door.
Emma: Nobody ever claims.
Heart: Nobody ever does. On with the music, then.

segments.flavor: the sounding, measuring how deep the night is
segments.text:
Heart: Time for the sounding. We drop the line and see how deep the night is.
Emma: Standing by.
Heart: [gentle] Twelve fathoms. No bottom found.
Emma: Twelve, and still nothing?
Heart: Thirty. Still nothing. The line is simply going.
Emma: At some point that is not a measurement, it is a mood.
Heart: [chuckle] No bottom found. Log it, and let the music run on.

segments.flavor: the Keeper's Inventory, what a lamp room actually holds
segments.text:
Heart: The Keeper's Inventory. What is actually in a lamp room, item by item.
Emma: Go.
Heart: One brass oil can. One cloth, only for the glass. One chair with a dent.
Emma: The dent is doing a lot of work in that sentence.
Heart: Nicole keeps a lamp room too, on the far side of the water.
Nicole: One kettle. One radio. One window that has been painted shut for decades.
Heart: Anything else?
Nicole: A list of everything I meant to fix. That is also an inventory.
Emma: [gentle] Every lamp room has one of those.
Heart: Every single one. Back out to the music.

segments.flavor: Distances, one thing and how far away it is
segments.text:
Heart: Distances. One thing, and how far away it is.
Emma: Which thing?
Heart: The nearest other light on this water is eleven miles out.
Emma: Can you see it?
Heart: On a clear night, yes. It blinks in a different rhythm than ours.
Emma: Do you ever signal it?
Heart: No. We keep our own time and let it keep its own.
Emma: That is either very peaceful or slightly sad.
Heart: Both, probably. Music, across eleven miles of dark water.

segments.flavor: the Slow Question, one question with no hurry on the answer
segments.text:
Heart: The Slow Question. One question, and no hurry at all on the answer.
Emma: Ready.
Heart: What is the last thing you do before sleep that nobody ever taught you?
Emma: I check a door I already checked. Twice.
Heart: Same. Everyone has one. A small ceremony that nobody wrote down.
Emma: Mine is the door. What is yours?
Heart: I look out at the water once, for no reason at all.
Emma: There is a reason.
Heart: Probably. Think about yours while this next one plays.
